event: Vera Chen's lab smells of ozone and clean metal, wrong for the Foundry District.
Forty by sixty feet: hand-labelled Flux arrays, resonance detectors, a wall of threaded notes.
Vera, silver-streaked bun and canvas apron, doesn't turn: "You're early." "It's 8:47."
He has bought instruments here twice; today he needs a density probe for a drift in his feedback.
Point-three percent a day: a self-reinforcing loop precise enough to see that, she notes.
Seventy-two hours unbroken, he says; she unlocks a cabinet and takes out a probe he's never seen.
A Rare Flux Density Probe, one of seven she has made: real-time density mapping within ten meters.
Six hundred Gold. Left alone the drift costs four percent in a week; the math favours buying.

changes.note: Vera's Flux Density Probe for 600 Gold

event: It will fix his drift, she says; how many in the zone run compound loops? None that he knows.
"None," Vera repeats. "I'd like to see it."
The walk to his warehouse takes eight minutes; her satchel clinks with instruments.
She stands in the middle of his array and looks, the way she once read collision data at Fermilab.
She raises the Cartographer's Lens to her eye and activates Substrate Analysis.
Thirty seconds of clinical calm; then her eyes tighten and her weight shifts forward.
"Walk me through the loop." Sentinel, Collector, Refinery, and the Enhancement Construct.
It gives upgrades to whichever construct has the best marginal return, mostly the Sentinel.
She asks again how long it has run unbroken: seventy-two hours, reinvesting without intervention.
"Your compound loop has a signature I've never seen in a player-built system."
She sits on his one free folding chair: there is a stat the Substrate doesn't show most people.
It measures how far your behaviour mirrors the Substrate's own processes. It is called Recursion.
He looks: below everything in his interface, wavering at the edge of sight, is Recursion 15.

changes.note: Recursion 15 shows in his window once Vera tells him where to look

event: His gut drops: for months he has been measured by a metric he didn't know existed.
Most people sit at zero to two, active fighters at zero; the highest she'd recorded was five.
He is at fifteen: three times her previous high, alone at the far end of the curve.
She has questions about why. "So do I."
He sits on his cot; she gives him space, like a doctor after a diagnosis.
He is building systems the Substrate considers kin; it thrills and sickens him in equal measure.
The stat keeps no history, she says; it climbs with sustained self-reinforcing behaviour.
His class may amplify it, but she can't confirm it: he is a sample size of one.
The air shimmers: level up, 17 to 18.
Intelligence to 61, Wisdom to 64, Willpower to 33: muscle memory now.
His loop's acceleration has crossed a threshold, Vera says; he'll level faster than he can think.
The Substrate runs on recursion, she says, and so does his loop: he runs its logic, not its code.
He writes Recursion and 15 in his notebook and underlines both twice. Pip pulses, quick and warm.
Twenty minutes later: level up, 18 to 19.

changes.note: Level 18 to 19 twenty minutes after the last

event: Intelligence 63, Wisdom 66, Willpower 34; HP 373, MP 864, Idle Yield 2.32x.
His Essence income is past eight thousand a day. "You're accelerating." "I know."
The acceleration accelerates because Recursion compounds too, he guesses. "Recursion is recursive."
Elegant or concerning, she hasn't decided. She pours black tea from a dented thermos.
She has three things to tell him, meant for several meetings; his score moved her timeline.
First: she Condensed at Level 26. The Substrate doesn't erase your pattern; it compresses it.
Every optimization and iteration is kept as an informational structure, folded denser.
The multiplier isn't a reward; it is what a denser pattern naturally puts out.
Condense is no power treadmill, he sees, but optimization applied to the player himself.
"You're not a player being reset. You're a process being optimized," Vera corrects.
Second: the Fracture Zones are not accidents. They are stress tests.
The Substrate is selecting for builders, whose systems scale; linear approaches fail first.
Everyone else is fuel, she says. He rejects it: Mira, Jin and the people of the zone are people.
But the Substrate's sorting may decide who survives.
Third, packing her satchel: he is being watched, and not only by the Iron Vanguard.
By the Substrate itself: he has had messages outside its usual vocabulary, hasn't he?
He thinks of the OBSERVED notices, and of WHAT ARE YOU BUILDING? in a ninety-six-hour session.
He nods. Those are attention, Vera says: he has become a process it considers significant.
"Either very good or very dangerous, and I am not yet sure which." She leaves.
He sits a long time. The Substrate cares about almost no one, and it cares about him.
His window: Loopweaver 19, Prestige 0, fifteen unspent skill points, Recursion 15.
With the probe he finds the feedback favouring the Sentinel, and corrects it in three minutes.
Three percent more efficient, and it will compound.
Under Recursion 15 he writes: Condense is compression; the Substrate is selecting for builders.
In the margin, smaller: It's watching.
Outside, a Vanguard patrol passes within two hundred meters of his Overgrowth constructs.
It rewards automation because it is automation, and measures recursion because it is recursive.
What are you building, he begins to understand, may mean: what are you becoming?
Pip flickers, warm and slow, like a cursor waiting for input.
Four threads weave over his cot now, denser and more recursive. Something is watching the graphs.
